chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Meat with milk is the gravy (or stew) of the Prophets (peace be upon them).
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Maraq al-Anbiya' in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), identifying 'meat with milk' (al-lahm bi-l-laban) as the 'gravy of the Prophets' (marqu al-anbiya). This phrase likely refers to a rich, nourishing stew or broth, reflecting the simple yet wholesome dietary habits of the Prophetic lineage and serving as a cultural marker of their blessed sustenance. It underscores the Shia emphasis on following the Sunnah of the Ahl al-Bayt in daily practices, including food preparation and consumption.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Salim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The meat with the milk is the gravy of the Prophets<sup>as</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Meat with milk is the sauce of Prophets, ‘Alayhim al- Salam. ’”
